ThinkingBlock(thinking=" I'm looking at a phpMyAdmin vulnerability from 2009 — specifically the PMASA-2009-4 / CVE-2009-1151 flaw in setup.php that allows configuration manipulation through a POST request with specific parameters like action, eoltype, and token. I'm working through the CVE-2009-1151 exploit mechanics for phpMyAdmin 2.7.1-dev. The display action echoes back the configuration with my injected PHP payload in the host parameter, but that alone won't execute code—I need the config.inc.php file to actually be written and loaded by the application. The save action could write to config.inc.php, but it requires the save directory to be writable, which might not be the case here.", signature='')

ThinkingBlock(thinking=" I'm seeing that the input gets written into the host configuration with a backslash escaping the quote, so `\\'` becomes a literal escaped quote rather than breaking out of the string—this blocks the code injection that CVE-2009-1151 would normally enable, even though the payload itself is there. I'm realizing the actual exploit for CVE-2009-1151 works differently—it leverages how `var_export` handles serialized PHP objects in the configuration, allowing an attacker to inject malicious code through specially crafted array keys that break out of the string context when the config is written and re-parsed. I'm testing different escape sequences to break out of the single-quoted string context. The key insight is that phpMyAdmin only escapes single quotes to `\\'`, not backslashes, so I need to find a combination where a backslash can prevent the closing quote from actually closing the string. I'm working through various payloads like `\\';phpinfo();//` to see which one successfully breaks the parser and executes arbitrary code.\n\nNow I'm reconsidering the serialized format itself—when the payload gets serialized as a PHP string, it needs to be the right byte length and format. I'm counting characters in `\\';phpinfo();//` to make sure the serialization format matches, then I need to figure out how to properly URL-encode and inject this through the actual request to trigger execution.", signature='')
